hypothesis: Repair generic quantity/clause token boundaries so canonical retrieval alternates retain complete alphanumeric technical designations instead of truncating at embedded quantity-like fragments.
why_now: Fresh corpus research confirms a structural evidence-loss bug in the accepted canonicalization layer. Semantic expansion, branded-model enrichment, candidate diversification, and selection-adjacent mechanisms have been neutral or unsafe.
expected_effect: Preserve complete designation evidence in additive retrieval queries without changing original-query retrieval, reranking, selection, or indexes.
success_signal: Affected real-tender rows retain complete canonical designations and improve viable family-consistent pre-rerank candidates, with no public or hidden gate regression.
candidate_hypotheses: Route affirmatively evidenced service-only or catalog-absent requests to uncertainty.
plan_summary: Created and strictly validated OpenSpec change `v2-cycle-01-query-evidence-preservation` with proposal, design, capability spec, and focused implementation/test tasks.
information_gain: Tests whether the successful canonicalization path is losing value through structural parsing loss rather than a remaining retrieval or reranking bottleneck.
